correctness.rationale: The hub-clock Poisson thinning is independent of all private-vertex clocks. In the frozen-hub process, all blades evolve independently and absorb at all ones almost surely. For a blade with z zeros, its down/up rates are z(r-z+1)/r and z(r-z)/r. The Feynman–Kac equations give the claimed tridiagonal determinant quotient with numerator product_z d_z=(r!)^2/r^r. The drift u_z-d_z=-z/r yields an integrated-zero expectation r^2. With all r_i bounded by R, the logarithms of the blade transforms have uniform second-order Taylor remainders, giving log p=-sum r_i^2/L+O_R(1/L). Independent full-labelled-state generator tests passed 40 cases with at most eight private vertices; symbolic calculations checked the transform and first derivative through private size six. All changes of state, not update attempts, are counted.

value.rationale: No-opinion-change persistence is a motivated observable in the historical voter-model literature. The exact factorization for arbitrary clique bouquets and its uniform finite-blade asymptotic give an explicit structural criterion: the size-biased private clique size controls hub persistence, even while the total hub degree grows. Adding only peripheral edges changes the star persistence limit e^-1 to e^-2 for friendship graphs at the same hub degree. Comparing to the classical fixation probability 1/(1+size-biased mean) shows that eventual victory and path persistence are quantitatively different. The result is an all-size infinite-family structural law, not a relabelled classical martingale or unmotivated finite invariant.
